documents.title: Ministerial Statement on Public Housing Affordability and Accessibility
documents.content: Mr Speaker, creating affordable and accessible homes for Singaporeans remains a key priority for the Government. We have ramped up the supply of Build-To-Order (BTO) flats and introduced the new Standard, Plus, and Prime classification to better reflect the locational attributes of public housing...
documents.summary: Minister addresses concerns on housing affordability and outlines the new BTO classification framework.
documents.speaker: Minister for National Development

documents.title: Enhancements to MediShield Life Scheme for 2026
documents.content: To better support Singaporeans with large hospital bills, the Ministry of Health will enhance MediShield Life claim limits starting 1 Jan 2026. This review ensures that the scheme remains relevant amidst rising medical costs and evolving healthcare needs...
documents.summary: MOH announces increased claim limits and premium adjustments for MediShield Life.
documents.speaker: Minister for Health

documents.title: Oral Answer to Question on Certificate of Entitlement (COE) Prices
documents.content: Mr Speaker, the COE system is designed to manage vehicle growth. The recent spike in Category A and B prices reflects strong demand. We are monitoring the market closely and have brought forward the deregistrations quota to smoothen supply...
documents.summary: Transport Minister responds to MP queries regarding record high COE premiums.
documents.speaker: Minister for Transport

documents.title: Changes to CPF Retirement Sum Scheme for 2026
documents.content: The Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) will be adjusted to $106,500 for members turning 55 in 2026. This adjustment accounts for long-term inflation and improvements in standard of living...
documents.summary: MOM announces adjustments to Basic, Full, and Enhanced Retirement Sums.
documents.speaker: Minister for Manpower

documents.title: Analysts: New housing grants likely to stabilize resale market
documents.content: Property analysts suggest that the enhanced housing grants announced in Parliament yesterday will help first-time buyers but may not immediately cool the resale market in mature estates. The new 'Plus' model is seen as a game changer...
documents.summary: CNA report on market reactions to the Prime/Plus/Standard HDB model.
documents.speaker: CNA Correspondent

documents.title: Straits Times: Public transport fare review 2025 concludes
documents.content: The Public Transport Council has concluded its 2025 fare review. Fares will see a marginal increase of 4 cents per journey due to rising energy costs, though concessions for seniors and students remain unchanged...
documents.summary: Report on the latest public transport fare adjustments.
documents.speaker: ST Transport Correspondent

documents.title: Second Reading of the Criminal Procedure (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill
documents.content: Mr Speaker, I beg to move, 'That the Bill be now read a second time.' This Bill introduces amendments to enhance the efficiency of our criminal justice system while ensuring fair trial rights...
documents.summary: Minister for Law introduces amendments to the Criminal Procedure Code.
documents.speaker: Minister for Law

documents.title: Forum: Ensuring MediShield Life stays affordable for the sandwich generation
documents.content: I refer to the recent announcement on MediShield Life premiums. While better coverage is welcome, many in the 'sandwich generation' worry about the cumulative impact of premium hikes for themselves and their aging parents...
documents.summary: Opinion piece discussing the financial impact of insurance premium hikes.
documents.speaker: Public Contributor

documents.title: Debate on Motion: Public Housing for the Future
documents.content: MP Louis Chua: While we support the new classification, we must ensure that the 'Plus' flats do not become inadvertently out of reach for the median income earner due to the clawback clauses...
documents.summary: Opposition MP raises concerns about the implementation of the new housing model.
documents.speaker: MP Louis Chua

documents.title: Expansion of the Cross Island Line (CRL)
documents.content: LTA has finalized the alignment for Phase 3 of the Cross Island Line. It will connect Jurong Lake District to Changi, significantly reducing travel time for commuters across the island...
documents.summary: LTA announces details for the next phase of the Cross Island Line MRT.
documents.speaker: LTA Spokesperson

documents.title: Oral Answer on PSLE Scoring and School Placement Flexibility
documents.content: Mr Speaker, Sir, the Ministry continues to review our education system to reduce excessive academic stress. The PSLE scoring system has been refined to focus on learning rather than competition. We are also exploring more flexible pathways for secondary school placements...
documents.summary: Education Minister addresses concerns on PSLE reforms and school placement system.
documents.speaker: Minister for Education

documents.title: Progressive Wage Model Extension to More Sectors
documents.content: To uplift the wages of lower-income workers, MOM will extend the Progressive Wage Model to the retail and food services sectors from 1 March 2026. This will benefit approximately 85,000 workers and ensure sustainable wage growth tied to skills upgrading...
documents.summary: MOM announces expansion of Progressive Wage Model to retail and F&B sectors.
documents.speaker: Minister for Manpower

documents.title: Singapore Green Plan 2030: Mid-Term Review
documents.content: Singapore is on track to meet several Green Plan 2030 targets. We have achieved 60% of our solar deployment goal and expanded our public EV charging network by 40%. However, we recognize the need to accelerate efforts in reducing household waste and industrial emissions...
documents.summary: Government presents progress update on Singapore Green Plan 2030 targets.
documents.speaker: Minister for Sustainability and the Environment

documents.title: Budget 2026: Support for SMEs and Innovation
documents.content: Mr Speaker, to support our SMEs in navigating economic headwinds, Budget 2026 will introduce enhanced productivity grants, extended the Enterprise Development Grant, and launch a new Innovation Voucher scheme worth $150 million...
documents.summary: Deputy Prime Minister announces key Budget 2026 measures for businesses.
documents.speaker: Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance

documents.title: Analysis: How Budget 2026 will affect middle-income households
documents.content: Economists say the targeted approach in Budget 2026 will provide relief to middle-income families facing rising costs. The new MediSave top-ups and enhanced childcare subsidies are seen as particularly helpful, though some analysts question if more could be done for the sandwich generation...
documents.summary: Economic analysis of Budget 2026 impact on households.
documents.speaker: TODAY Economics Correspondent

documents.title: Foreign worker quota adjustments spark debate among employers
documents.content: Business groups have raised concerns over the tightened foreign worker dependency ratios announced by MOM. While acknowledging the need to uplift local employment, industry leaders say the construction and marine sectors need transitional support...
documents.summary: Business sector responds to new foreign worker policy changes.
documents.speaker: BT Labour Correspondent

documents.title: New full-day pre-school programme to launch in 2027
documents.content: MOE will pilot a new full-day pre-school programme at 20 MOE Kindergartens starting in 2027. This addresses working parents' needs and aligns with recommendations from the recent Early Childhood Care and Education Review Committee...
documents.summary: MOE announces expansion of full-day kindergarten programme.
documents.speaker: CNA Education Correspondent

documents.title: Parliament approves Carbon Tax (Amendment) Bill
documents.content: After two days of debate, Parliament has passed the Carbon Tax (Amendment) Bill. The carbon tax will increase from $25 per tonne to $50 per tonne in 2026, with a further rise to $80 per tonne by 2030. Revenue will fund green transition initiatives and support affected industries...
documents.summary: Parliament passes legislation to raise carbon tax rates progressively.
documents.speaker: Parliament Reporter
